# Module interfaces

<!-- Generated by scripts/export_module_interfaces.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Each feature module in `app/modules/` owns its tables and is used by other
modules only through its `service.py`, whose functions return dataclasses. This
reference lists, for every module, the tables it owns, the modules it may call
and be called by (`ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES`), the events it publishes or reacts to,
its `/api/v1` routes and its public service interface. See
`docs/architecture.md` for the rules and `ENABLED_MODULES` for serving a subset.

| Module | Owns tables | May call | Called by | Routes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [accounts](#accounts) | `users`, `profile_pictures` | – | `admin`, `analytics`, `channels`, `chat`, `llm`, `materials`, `moderation_queue`, `notifications`, `profiles`, `questions`, `quizzes`, `reputation` | 6 |
| [admin](#admin) | – | `accounts`, `channels`, `materials`, `moderation`, `notifications`, `questions` | – | 8 |
| [analytics](#analytics) | `performance_attempts`, `performance_topics`, `recommendation_opens` | `accounts`, `channels`, `materials`, `questions`, `quizzes` | – | 4 |
| [channels](#channels) | `channels`, `channel_memberships`, `channel_posts` | `accounts`, `moderation`, `notifications` | `admin`, `analytics`, `chat`, `llm`, `materials`, `moderation_queue`, `questions`, `quizzes` | 15 |
| [chat](#chat) | `channel_messages`, `conversations`, `conversation_participants`, `direct_messages`, `user_blocks` | `accounts`, `channels`, `materials`, `moderation`, `questions`, `quizzes` | – | 12 |
| [llm](#llm) | `llm_requests`, `adaptive_sessions` | `accounts`, `channels`, `moderation`, `questions`, `quizzes` | `moderation_queue` | 15 |

## accounts

Accounts module (FR-01).

- **Owns tables:** `users`, `profile_pictures`
- **May call:** –
- **Called by:** `admin`, `analytics`, `channels`, `chat`, `llm`, `materials`, `moderation_queue`, `notifications`, `profiles`, `questions`, `quizzes`, `reputation`
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** –
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/accounts/README.md`](../app/modules/accounts/README.md)

### Routes

- `POST /api/v1/accounts/register`
- `POST /api/v1/accounts/login`
- `GET /api/v1/accounts/me`
- `GET /api/v1/accounts/me/permissions`
- `GET /api/v1/accounts/admin/users`
- `GET /api/v1/accounts/session-policy`

### Service functions

- `create_user(db, *, email, display_name, password, role, username) -> UserSummary` — Create a user with a hashed password. Emails and usernames are stored lower-cased.
- `get_user(db, user_id) -> UserSummary | None` — Return the account's summary, or None if no user has that id.
- `get_users(db, user_ids) -> dict[int, UserSummary]` — Several users at once, keyed by id; unknown ids are left out (S13.1 leaderboard).
- `get_user_by_email(db, email) -> UserSummary | None` — Return the summary of the account with this email (case-insensitive), or None.
- `get_users_by_username(db, usernames) -> dict[str, UserSummary]` — Users by username (case-insensitive), keyed by the lower-cased name (S14.1 mentions).
- `set_suspended(db, user_id, suspended) -> None` — Suspend or reinstate an account; raises LookupError for an unknown user.
- `add_reputation(db, user_id, points) -> None` — Adjust the cached reputation total (the reputation module owns the event log).
- `register_account(db, *, display_name, username, email, password) -> AccountDetails` — Register a Student, rejecting a username or email that is already in use.
- `authenticate(db, identifier, password) -> UserSummary | None` — Return the user if ``identifier`` (username or email) and ``password`` match.
- `get_account(db, user_id) -> AccountDetails | None` — Return the account's details, or None if no user has that id.
- `list_accounts(db) -> list[AccountDetails]` — Every account, oldest first. Callers must hold ``Capability.USER_MANAGE``.
- `count_accounts(db) -> int` — Return the number of accounts, counted in the database.
- `count_suspended_accounts(db) -> int` — How many accounts are suspended, counted in the database (NFR-05).
- `get_profile(db, user_id) -> ProfileDetails | None` — Return the user's profile, or None if no user has that id.
- `update_profile(db, user_id, *, display_name, bio, institution) -> ProfileDetails` — Change only the fields passed. Blank bio or institution clears it. Caller commits.
- `detect_image_type(data) -> str | None` — The image type from the file's leading bytes, or ``None`` if it isn't one we accept.
- `set_profile_picture(db, user_id, data) -> ProfileDetails` — Validate and store ``data`` as the user's picture, replacing any earlier one.
- `remove_profile_picture(db, user_id) -> ProfileDetails` — Delete the user's profile picture if any and return the updated profile.
- `get_profile_picture(db, user_id) -> ProfilePictureData | None` — Return the stored profile picture bytes and type, or None if there is none.

### Data types

- `UserSummary(id, display_name, role, is_suspended, username)`
- `AccountDetails(id, username, email, display_name, role, created_at, is_suspended)` — What the account owner, or an admin, may see about an account.
- `DuplicateAccountError(Exception)` — A username or email is already registered.
- `ProfileDetails(id, username, display_name, role, bio, institution, created_at, picture_updated_at)` — The editable, publicly visible part of an account. Email is not included.
- `ProfilePictureData(content_type, data, updated_at)`
- `InvalidPictureError(Exception)` — An uploaded profile picture was refused; ``str(exc)`` is the user-facing reason.

Also re-exported from the module's internals: `Capability`, `capabilities_for`, `current_user`, `require_capability`, `require_roles`.

## admin

Admin module (FR-14, story S14.2).

- **Owns tables:** –
- **May call:** `accounts`, `channels`, `materials`, `moderation`, `notifications`, `questions`
- **Called by:** –
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** –
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/admin/README.md`](../app/modules/admin/README.md)

### Routes

- `GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard`
- `GET /api/v1/admin/users`
- `POST /api/v1/admin/users/{user_id}/suspend`
- `POST /api/v1/admin/users/{user_id}/reinstate`
- `GET /api/v1/admin/channel-requests`
- `GET /api/v1/admin/reports`
- `POST /api/v1/admin/content/{target_type}/{target_id}/remove`
- `GET /api/v1/admin/audit-log`

### Service functions

- `suspend_user(db, *, admin_id, user_id, reason) -> AccountDetails` — Suspend an account: it can no longer log in, and its open sessions stop working.
- `reinstate_user(db, *, admin_id, user_id, reason) -> AccountDetails` — Lift a suspension; the user can log in again.
- `remove_content(db, *, admin_id, target_type, target_id, reason) -> RemovedContent` — Remove a material or question platform-wide for a rule violation.
- `dashboard(db) -> DashboardSummary` — Return the admin dashboard counts (users, suspensions, requests, reports, flags).

### Data types

- `AdminActionError(Exception)` — An admin action that cannot be carried out; ``str(error)`` is the wording.
- `NotFound(AdminActionError)`
- `NotAllowed(AdminActionError)`
- `Conflict(AdminActionError)`
- `RemovedContent(target_type, target_id, title, poster_id, channel_id, resolved_report_ids, notified, audit_entry_id)`
- `DashboardSummary(total_users, suspended_users, pending_channel_requests, open_reports, flagged_items)` — What the admin dashboard opens with: the work waiting for an admin.

## analytics

Analytics module (FR-12).

- **Owns tables:** `performance_attempts`, `performance_topics`, `recommendation_opens`
- **May call:** `accounts`, `channels`, `materials`, `questions`, `quizzes`
- **Called by:** –
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** `ATTEMPT_SCORED`
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/analytics/README.md`](../app/modules/analytics/README.md)

### Routes

- `GET /api/v1/analytics/dashboard`
- `GET /api/v1/analytics/reconciliation`
- `GET /api/v1/analytics/recommendations`
- `POST /api/v1/analytics/recommendations/opened`

### Service functions

- `recompute(db, user_id) -> dict[tuple[str, str], TopicTotals]` — The user's per-topic figures derived from raw attempts alone (writes nothing).
- `stored(db, user_id) -> dict[tuple[str, str], TopicTotals]` — The user's per-topic figures as currently stored.
- `summary_for_user(db, user_id) -> PerformanceSummary` — Overall attempt count and points from the stored figures.
- `record_attempt(db, attempt_id) -> None` — Fold one scored attempt into its user's figures (the ``ATTEMPT_SCORED`` handler).
- `sync_user(db, user_id) -> int` — Reconcile the user's stored figures with their raw attempts; returns rows fixed.
- `rebuild_user(db, user_id) -> None` — Discard the user's stored figures and rebuild them from raw attempts.
- `classify(attempts, accuracy) -> Standing` — Strong, developing or weak by accuracy; too few attempts are never labelled.
- `trend(points) -> Trend` — Least-squares line through the attempt percentages, in attempt order.
- `dashboard(db, user_id) -> Dashboard` — Performance by subject and topic with trends and strong/weak topics.
- `recommendations_for(db, user_id, *, limit)` — Materials, questions and quizzes for the user's weak topics, best first.
- `record_recommendation_open(db, user_id, item_type, item_id) -> None` — Remember that the user opened a recommended item, to de-prioritise it later.

### Data types

- `Standing(StrEnum)`
- `Direction(StrEnum)`
- `TopicTotals(subject, topic, attempts, total_score, total_possible)`
- `PerformanceSummary(attempts, total_score, total_possible)`
- `TopicPerformance(subject, topic, attempts, total_score, total_possible, accuracy, standing)`
- `TrendPoint(attempt_id, quiz_id, quiz_title, subject, topic, submitted_at, percentage, running_accuracy)`
- `Trend(points, slope, direction, line_start, line_end)`
- `SubjectPerformance(subject, attempts, total_score, total_possible, accuracy, topics, trend)`
- `Dashboard(attempts, total_score, total_possible, accuracy, subjects, trend, strengths, weak_areas, not_enough_data, empty_message, min_attempts, strong_at, weak_below, topics)`

## channels

Channels module (FR-02, FR-03).

- **Owns tables:** `channels`, `channel_memberships`, `channel_posts`
- **May call:** `accounts`, `moderation`, `notifications`
- **Called by:** `admin`, `analytics`, `chat`, `llm`, `materials`, `moderation_queue`, `questions`, `quizzes`
- **Publishes events:** `CHANNEL_POST_CREATED`
- **Subscribes to events:** –
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/channels/README.md`](../app/modules/channels/README.md)

### Routes

- `POST /api/v1/channels`
- `GET /api/v1/channels`
- `GET /api/v1/channels/mine`
- `GET /api/v1/channels/requests`
- `GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}`
- `POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/approve`
- `POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/reject`
- `POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/join`
- `POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/leave`
- `GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/members`
- `DELETE /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/members/{user_id}`
- `POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/posts`
- `GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/posts`
- `PATCH /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/posts/{post_id}`
- `DELETE /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/posts/{post_id}`

### Service functions

- `create_channel(db, *, name, created_by, channel_type, subject, topic, description) -> ChannelSummary` — Create a channel and make its creator the owner.
- `set_approval(db, channel_id, status) -> None` — Set an authorized channel's approval status; raises LookupError if unknown.
- `get_channel(db, channel_id) -> ChannelSummary | None` — Return the channel's summary, or None if no channel has that id.
- `add_member(db, channel_id, user_id, role) -> None` — Add the user to the channel with ``role``; does nothing if already a member.
- `member_roles(db, user_id, channel_ids) -> dict[int, MemberRole]` — The user's role in each of these channels they belong to, in one query (NFR-05).
- `describe_channels(db, channel_ids) -> dict[int, ChannelSummary]` — Several channels with their member counts, keyed by id; unknown ids are left out.
- `member_role(db, channel_id, user_id) -> MemberRole | None` — The user's role in the channel, or ``None`` if they are not a member.
- `is_member(db, channel_id, user_id) -> bool` — Return whether the user belongs to the channel in any role.
- `describe_channel(db, channel_id) -> ChannelSummary | None` — A channel with its member count, for channel pages and lists.
- `is_visible_to(summary, viewer_id, viewer_is_admin) -> bool` — Approved channels are visible to everyone; a pending or rejected Authorized Channel only to the person who requested it and to admins.
- `list_channels(db, *, viewer_id, viewer_is_admin, query, channel_type) -> list[ChannelSummary]` — Channels the viewer may see, optionally searched by name, subject or topic.
- `pending_requests(db) -> list[ChannelSummary]` — Authorized Channel requests awaiting an admin decision, oldest first.
- `can_manage_members(role) -> bool` — Whether a channel role may remove members at all (creator or moderator).
- `can_remove(actor_role, target_role) -> bool` — Return whether a member in ``actor_role`` may remove one in ``target_role``.
- `remove_member(db, channel_id, user_id) -> bool` — Delete a membership. Returns ``False`` if the user was not a member.
- `list_members(db, channel_id) -> list[MemberSummary]` — A channel's members, owner first, then moderators, then by join order.
- `channels_for_member(db, user_id) -> list[tuple[ChannelSummary, MemberRole]]` — My Channels: every channel the user belongs to, with their role in it.
- `manages_official_content(summary, *, is_member, has_capability, is_admin) -> bool` — Whether a user may add, edit and remove official content in this channel.
- `create_post(db, channel_id, author_id, body) -> PostSummary` — Add a discussion post to a channel. Caller checks membership and commits.
- `get_post(db, channel_id, post_id) -> PostSummary | None` — Return the post if it belongs to the channel, otherwise None.
- `list_posts(db, channel_id, *, limit, offset) -> tuple[list[PostSummary], int]` — A channel's posts, newest first, and how many there are.
- `edit_post(db, post_id, body) -> PostSummary` — Replace a post's text and mark it edited. Caller checks authorship and commits.
- `delete_post(db, post_id) -> None` — Delete the post if it exists.

### Data types

- `ChannelSummary(id, name, channel_type, approval_status, subject, topic, description, created_by, created_at, member_count)`
- `MemberSummary(user_id, role, joined_at)`
- `PostSummary(id, channel_id, author_id, body, created_at, edited_at)`

## chat

Chat module (FR-10, FR-11).

- **Owns tables:** `channel_messages`, `conversations`, `conversation_participants`, `direct_messages`, `user_blocks`
- **May call:** `accounts`, `channels`, `materials`, `moderation`, `questions`, `quizzes`
- **Called by:** –
- **Publishes events:** `CHANNEL_MESSAGE_POSTED`
- **Subscribes to events:** –
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/chat/README.md`](../app/modules/chat/README.md)

### Routes

- `POST /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages`
- `GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages`
- `GET /api/v1/channels/{channel_id}/messages/{message_id}/replies`
- `POST /api/v1/conversations`
- `GET /api/v1/conversations`
- `GET /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}`
- `POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`
- `GET /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`
- `POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages/{message_id}/reports`
- `GET /api/v1/blocks`
- `PUT /api/v1/blocks/{user_id}`
- `DELETE /api/v1/blocks/{user_id}`

### Service functions

- `post_channel_message(db, *, channel_id, sender_id, body, parent_id, shared_resource) -> int` — Store a channel message (optionally a reply or a shared resource); returns its id.
- `mentioned_members(db, channel_id, body) -> list[int]` — The channel members a message names with @username, in order (S14.1).
- `channel_history(db, channel_id, limit) -> list[MessageView]` — Return the channel's visible messages, oldest first, up to ``limit``.
- `get_channel_message(db, channel_id, message_id) -> MessageView | None` — One message of a channel's chat, or None if it is not there (or was deleted).
- `thread_root(db, channel_id, message_id) -> int | None` — The message a reply to ``message_id`` belongs under, or None if it can't be replied to.
- `thread_summaries(db, message_ids) -> dict[int, ThreadSummary]` — Visible reply count and latest reply time for each message that has replies.
- `channel_messages_page(db, channel_id, *, limit, before, after, thread_of) -> tuple[list[MessageView], bool]` — A page of a channel's chat in the order the server accepted the messages (S10.1).
- `is_blocked(db, sender_id, recipient_id) -> bool` — True if either user has blocked the other.
- `find_conversation(db, user_a, user_b) -> int | None` — The id of the one-to-one conversation between two users, if there is one.
- `open_conversation(db, user_a, user_b) -> int` — Return the id of the one-to-one conversation between two users, creating it.
- `send_direct_message(db, *, conversation_id, sender_id, body, shared_resource) -> int` — Store a message in a conversation (optionally sharing a resource); returns its id.
- `conversation_participants(db, conversation_id) -> list[int]` — The user ids taking part in a conversation (empty if it doesn't exist).
- `get_conversation(db, conversation_id, user_id) -> ConversationSummary | None` — The conversation as ``user_id`` sees it, or None if they are not in it.
- `conversations_for(db, user_id) -> list[ConversationSummary]` — The user's conversations, most recent activity first.
- `blocks_involving(db, user_id) -> tuple[set[int], set[int]]` — Who the user has blocked, and who has blocked them, in one query (NFR-05).
- `get_direct_message(db, message_id) -> DirectMessageView | None` — Return the direct message, or None if no message has that id.
- `direct_messages_page(db, conversation_id, *, limit, before, after) -> tuple[list[DirectMessageView], bool]` — A page of a conversation in the order the server accepted the messages.
- `has_blocked(db, blocker_id, blocked_id) -> bool` — True if ``blocker_id`` has blocked ``blocked_id`` (one direction only).
- `block_user(db, blocker_id, blocked_id, reason) -> bool` — Block a user. Returns False if they were already blocked (nothing changes).
- `unblock_user(db, blocker_id, blocked_id) -> bool` — Lift a block. Returns False if there was none.
- `blocked_by(db, blocker_id) -> list[int]` — The ids of the users ``blocker_id`` has blocked, earliest first.

### Data types

- `MessageView(id, sender_id, body, parent_id, shared_resource_type, shared_resource_id, created_at)`
- `ThreadSummary(reply_count, last_reply_at)` — What the main stream shows under a message that has replies (S10.2).
- `DirectMessageView(id, conversation_id, sender_id, body, shared_resource_type, shared_resource_id, created_at)`
- `ConversationSummary(id, other_user_id, created_at, last_message)` — A one-to-one conversation as one of its two participants sees it.

### Data types

## materials

Materials module (FR-04).

- **Owns tables:** `study_materials`, `material_reviews`, `material_files`
- **May call:** `accounts`, `channels`, `moderation`, `reputation`
- **Called by:** `admin`, `analytics`, `chat`, `moderation_queue`, `profiles`
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** –
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/materials/README.md`](../app/modules/materials/README.md)

### Routes

- `POST /api/v1/materials`
- `GET /api/v1/materials`
- `GET /api/v1/materials/{material_id}`
- `GET /api/v1/materials/{material_id}/preview`
- `GET /api/v1/materials/{material_id}/download`
- `PUT /api/v1/materials/{material_id}/review`
- `GET /api/v1/materials/{material_id}/reviews`
- `PUT /api/v1/materials/{material_id}/helpful`
- `DELETE /api/v1/materials/{material_id}/helpful`
- `POST /api/v1/materials/{material_id}/reports`
- `PATCH /api/v1/materials/{material_id}`
- `DELETE /api/v1/materials/{material_id}`

### Service functions

- `create_material(db, *, uploader_id, title, material_type, subject, topic, semester, channel_id, url, file_path, description, is_official) -> MaterialSummary` — Store a study material's metadata and return its summary.
- `get_material(db, material_id) -> MaterialSummary | None` — Return an active material's summary, or None if missing or removed.
- `get_materials(db, material_ids) -> dict[int, MaterialSummary]` — Several active materials at once, keyed by id (NFR-05); like ``get_material``, removed or unknown ids are left out.
- `set_removed(db, material_id, removed) -> None` — Remove or restore a material (moderation); raises LookupError if unknown.
- `update_material(db, material_id, **changes) -> MaterialSummary` — Change an active material's details (S03.1). Caller validates and commits.
- `count_uploaded_by(db, user_id) -> int` — How many materials the user contributed that are still active.
- `recent_uploaded_by(db, user_id, limit) -> list[MaterialContribution]` — Return the user's latest active uploads, newest first.
- `file_too_large_message(max_bytes) -> str` — Return the user-facing message for a file over ``max_bytes``.
- `clean_filename(filename) -> str` — The file's base name with any client path and control characters removed.
- `validate_file(filename, data, max_bytes) -> tuple[str, str]` — Check an upload's size and type; return its clean name and content type.
- `attach_file(db, material_id, *, filename, content_type, data) -> MaterialFileInfo` — Store a validated file for a material, replacing any earlier one. Caller commits.
- `describe_material(db, material_id) -> MaterialSummary | None` — An active material with its tags and file details, or ``None``.
- `checksum(data) -> str` — Return the SHA-256 hex digest stored with an uploaded file (NFR-04).
- `get_material_file(db, material_id) -> MaterialFileData | None` — The bytes of an active material's file, or ``None`` if it has no file.
- `search_materials(db, *, channel_ids, include_general, query, subject, topic, semester, material_type, is_official, limit, offset) -> MaterialPage` — Active materials matching every filter given, newest first.
- `feedback_for(db, material_ids, viewer_id) -> dict[int, MaterialFeedback]` — Rating average and count, review count and helpful count per material.
- `rate_material(db, material_id, user_id, rating, review) -> MaterialFeedback` — Save the user's 1-5 rating and optional review text. Caller commits.
- `set_helpful(db, material_id, user_id, helpful) -> MaterialFeedback` — Mark (or unmark) the material helpful for this user. Caller commits.
- `list_reviews(db, material_id, *, limit, offset) -> tuple[list[MaterialReviewEntry], int]` — Written reviews of a material, newest first, and how many there are.

### Data types

- `MaterialFileInfo(filename, content_type, size_bytes, sha256)` — What is known about a material's file without loading its bytes.
- `MaterialSummary(id, title, subject, topic, material_type, channel_id, semester, description, uploader_id, created_at, is_official, url, file)`
- `MaterialContribution(id, title, created_at)` — One material the user contributed, for their profile's history (S01.2).
- `InvalidMaterialFileError(Exception)` — An uploaded file was refused; ``str(exc)`` is the user-facing reason.
- `MaterialFileData(filename, content_type, data, sha256)`
- `DamagedFileError(Exception)` — A stored file no longer matches the checksum taken at upload (NFR-04).
- `MaterialPage(items, total)`
- `MaterialFeedback(rating_average, rating_count, review_count, helpful_count, my_rating, my_review, marked_helpful)` — A material's rating summary, plus the viewer's own feedback when known.
- `MaterialReviewEntry(id, user_id, rating, review, marked_helpful, created_at)` — One user's written review of a material.

## moderation

Moderation module (FR-13, FR-14).

- **Owns tables:** `reports`, `moderation_actions`
- **May call:** –
- **Called by:** `admin`, `channels`, `chat`, `llm`, `materials`, `moderation_queue`, `questions`
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** –

### Routes

None.

### Service functions

- `file_report(db, *, reporter_id, target_type, target_id, reason, details, channel_id) -> int` — File an open report against a piece of content; returns the report id.
- `get_report(db, report_id) -> ReportSummary | None` — Return the report's summary, or None if no report has that id.
- `find_open_report(db, *, reporter_id, target_type, target_id) -> int | None` — The reporter's still-open report on this target, if any (avoids duplicates).
- `open_reports(db, channel_id) -> list[int]` — Return the ids of open reports, oldest first, optionally for one channel.
- `resolve_report(db, report_id, *, moderator_id, dismissed, note) -> None` — Close a report as resolved or dismissed by ``moderator_id``.
- `log_action(db, *, actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, report_id, note) -> int` — Append a moderation or admin action to the audit log; returns its id.
- `report_queue(db, *, channel_ids) -> list[QueueItem]` — Open reports grouped by what they report, oldest first.
- `reports_on(db, target_type, target_id) -> QueueItem` — Every report on one item, open or closed, oldest first.
- `close_reports_on(db, *, target_type, target_id, moderator_id, dismissed, note) -> list[int]` — Resolve (or dismiss) every open report on an item at once; returns their ids.
- `reports_filed_by(db, reporter_id, limit) -> list[ReportSummary]` — A reporter's own reports, newest first, so they can follow what happened.
- `actions_on(db, target_type, target_id) -> list[ActionEntry]` — The moderation history of one item, oldest first.
- `flagged_targets(db, target_type) -> list[FlaggedTarget]` — Open reports grouped by what they report, most-reported first (ST_28).
- `count_open_reports(db) -> int` — Return the number of open reports, counted in the database.
- `audit_log(db, *, limit, before, target_type, target_id) -> tuple[list[AuditEntry], bool]` — Admin actions newest first, paged with ``before=<oldest id shown>``.

### Data types

- `ReportSummary(id, reporter_id, target_type, target_id, reason, details, channel_id, status, created_at)` — A report as filed: what was reported, by whom, why and when.
- `ReportEntry(id, reporter_id, reason, details, status, created_at, resolved_by, resolved_at, resolution_note)` — One report in the queue: who filed it, why, and how it was closed.
- `QueueItem(target_type, target_id, channel_id, reports)` — Every open report on one piece of content, grouped so duplicates show once.
- `ActionEntry(id, actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, report_id, note, created_at)` — One recorded moderation action: who did what to which item, and when.
- `FlaggedTarget(target_type, target_id, channel_id, report_count, reasons, first_reported_at, last_reported_at)` — One reported item in the admin queue: every open report on it, grouped.
- `AuditEntry(id, actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, report_id, note, created_at)` — One admin action as the audit log records it: actor, action, target and time.

Notifications module (FR-14).

- **Owns tables:** `notifications`, `notification_preferences`
- **May call:** `accounts`
- **Called by:** `admin`, `channels`
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** `CHANNEL_MESSAGE_POSTED`, `CHANNEL_POST_CREATED`, `QUIZ_PUBLISHED`

### Routes

- `GET /api/v1/notifications`
- `GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count`
- `GET /api/v1/notifications/preferences`
- `PUT /api/v1/notifications/preferences`
- `POST /api/v1/notifications/read-all`
- `POST /api/v1/notifications/{notification_id}/read`

### Service functions

- `is_enabled(db, user_id, kind) -> bool` — Notifications are on unless the user has turned that kind off.
- `set_preference(db, user_id, kind, enabled) -> None` — Switch one notification category on or off for the user.
- `notify(db, *, user_id, kind, title, body, link) -> int | None` — Create a notification if the user wants this kind; returns its id or ``None``.
- `notifications_for(db, user_id, *, limit, unread_only) -> list[NotificationView]` — A user's notifications, newest first.
- `unread_count(db, user_id) -> int` — Return how many of the user's notifications are unread.
- `mark_read(db, user_id, notification_id) -> bool` — Mark one of the user's notifications read; False if it isn't theirs.
- `mark_all_read(db, user_id) -> int` — Mark every unread notification of the user read; returns how many changed.
- `preferences(db, user_id) -> dict[NotificationKind, bool]` — Every category with whether the user receives it (on unless switched off).

### Data types

- `NotificationView(id, kind, title, body, link, is_read, created_at)`

## questions

Questions module (FR-05, FR-07).

- **Owns tables:** `questions`, `question_ratings`
- **May call:** `accounts`, `channels`, `moderation`, `reputation`
- **Called by:** `admin`, `analytics`, `chat`, `llm`, `moderation_queue`, `profiles`, `quizzes`
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** –
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/questions/README.md`](../app/modules/questions/README.md)

### Routes

- `POST /api/v1/questions`
- `GET /api/v1/questions`
- `GET /api/v1/questions/{question_id}`
- `PUT /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/rating`
- `POST /api/v1/questions/{question_id}/reports`

### Service functions

- `create_question(db, *, author_id, subject, topic, difficulty, question_type, text, options, correct_answer, explanation, expected_concepts, channel_id, source) -> QuestionView` — Add a question. LLM-generated questions start as drafts for review (FR-07).
- `get_questions(db, ids) -> dict[int, QuestionView]` — Fetch questions by id, keyed by id (missing ids are simply absent).
- `find_questions(db, *, subject, topic, difficulty, channel_id, limit) -> list[QuestionView]` — Published questions matching every filter given.
- `count_authored_by(db, user_id) -> int` — How many published questions the user wrote; drafts and removed ones don't count.
- `recent_authored_by(db, user_id, limit) -> list[QuestionContribution]` — Return the user's latest published questions, newest first.
- `get_question_owner(db, question_id) -> QuestionOwner | None` — A published question's author and headline; None if missing or not published.
- `get_question_owners(db, question_ids) -> dict[int, QuestionOwner]` — ``get_question_owner`` for several questions in one query (NFR-05).
- `set_removed(db, question_id, removed) -> None` — Take a question off the platform (or put it back); it keeps its history.
- `get_bank_question(db, question_id, viewer_id) -> BankQuestion | None` — One question with its rating summary, whatever its status (callers check access).
- `get_bank_questions(db, question_ids, viewer_id) -> dict[int, BankQuestion]` — ``get_bank_question`` for several questions with one query per kind of data (NFR-05); unknown ids are left out.
- `search_bank(db, *, keyword, subject, topic, difficulty, question_type, channel_id, viewer_id, limit, offset) -> list[BankQuestion]` — Published questions in one bank, newest first.
- `published_in_scope(db, *, channel_ids, include_general, subject, topic, exclude_author_id, limit) -> list[BankQuestion]` — Published questions from the general bank and the given channels' banks (S12.2).
- `rate_question(db, question_id, user_id, rating) -> BankQuestion` — Save the user's 1-5 rating; rating again replaces their earlier rating.
- `quiz_candidates(db, *, subject, topic, difficulty, channel_id) -> list[BankQuestion]` — Published questions a quiz may use, oldest first.
- `update_draft(db, question_id, *, text, options, correct_answer, explanation) -> QuestionView` — Save a reviewer's correction to a draft; it stays a draft until approved.
- `publish_draft(db, question_id) -> None` — Approve a draft: it joins its bank and becomes usable in quizzes.
- `discard_draft(db, question_id) -> None` — Reject a draft. It is kept only as a removed record and never reaches a bank, a search result or a quiz, all of which use published questions only.

### Data types

- `QuestionView(id, subject, topic, difficulty, question_type, text, options, correct_answer, explanation, expected_concepts)`
- `QuestionContribution(id, title, created_at)` — One question the user contributed, for their profile's history (S01.2).
- `QuestionOwner(id, author_id, headline, channel_id, ai_generated)` — Who posted a published question and how to name it (S14.2 content removal).
- `BankQuestion(question, channel_id, author_id, source, status, created_at, rating_average, rating_count, my_rating)` — A question as the bank presents it: content, scope, provenance and ratings.
- `NotADraftError(Exception)` — The question has already been reviewed (approved or rejected).

## quizzes

Quizzes module (FR-05, FR-06, FR-07).

- **Owns tables:** `quizzes`, `quiz_questions`, `quiz_attempts`, `attempt_answers`
- **May call:** `accounts`, `channels`, `questions`
- **Called by:** `analytics`, `chat`, `llm`, `profiles`
- **Publishes events:** `ATTEMPT_SCORED`, `QUIZ_PUBLISHED`
- **Subscribes to events:** –
- **Notes:** [`app/modules/quizzes/README.md`](../app/modules/quizzes/README.md)

### Routes

- `POST /api/v1/quizzes/preview`
- `POST /api/v1/quizzes`
- `GET /api/v1/quizzes`
- `GET /api/v1/quizzes/{quiz_id}`
- `POST /api/v1/quizzes/{quiz_id}/publish`
- `POST /api/v1/quizzes/{quiz_id}/attempts`
- `GET /api/v1/attempts`
- `GET /api/v1/attempts/{attempt_id}`
- `PUT /api/v1/attempts/{attempt_id}/answers`
- `POST /api/v1/attempts/{attempt_id}/submit`

### Service functions

- `create_quiz(db, *, creator_id, title, subject, topic, difficulty, duration_minutes, question_ids, channel_id, publish, adaptive) -> int` — Create a quiz from question-bank questions in the given order; returns its id.
- `start_attempt(db, quiz_id, user_id) -> int` — Start an attempt with its time limit fixed from the quiz duration (S06.1).
- `open_attempt_for(db, quiz_id, user_id) -> int | None` — The user's attempt at this quiz that is still running, if any (S09.1 resume).
- `submit_attempt(db, attempt_id, responses) -> AttemptResult` — Store answers, score objective questions and close the attempt (FR-06).
- `get_attempt_result(db, attempt_id) -> AttemptResult` — Return an attempt's score summary; raises LookupError if unknown.
- `attempts_for_user(db, user_id) -> list[AttemptResult]` — Submitted attempts, oldest first (used by analytics, FR-12).
- `scored_attempt(db, attempt_id) -> ScoredAttempt | None` — The attempt as analytics sees it, or ``None`` if it is missing or still running.
- `scored_attempts_for_user(db, user_id) -> list[ScoredAttempt]` — Every submitted attempt of the user, oldest first (ties broken by id).
- `close_expired_attempts(db, user_id) -> int` — Auto-submit the user's attempts whose time ran out; returns how many closed.
- `published_in_scope(db, *, channel_ids, include_general, subject, topic, exclude_creator_id, limit) -> list[QuizListing]` — Published quizzes with questions, general and in the given channels.
- `describe_quiz(db, quiz_id) -> QuizInfo | None` — One quiz's current details, whatever its status (callers check access).
- `attempted_quiz_ids(db, user_id) -> set[int]` — Quizzes the user has submitted at least one attempt at.
- `answered_question_ids(db, user_id) -> set[int]` — Questions the user has answered in a submitted attempt.
- `count_created_by(db, user_id) -> int` — How many published quizzes the user created; drafts and removed ones don't count.
- `recent_created_by(db, user_id, limit) -> list[QuizContribution]` — Return the user's latest published quizzes, newest first.
- `add_quiz_question(db, quiz_id, question_id) -> int` — Append a question to an adaptive quiz as it is served; returns its position.
- `adaptive_history(db, attempt_id) -> list[ServedQuestion]` — Questions served so far with their difficulty and result, in serving order.
- `answer_adaptive(db, attempt_id, question_id, response) -> AdaptiveAnswer` — Score the current question's answer immediately (deterministic scoring).
- `finish_attempt(db, attempt_id) -> AttemptOutcome` — Close the attempt and return its result.
- `attempt_outcome(db, attempt_id) -> AttemptOutcome | None` — The result of a submitted attempt, or ``None`` while it is still running.
- `attempt_owner(db, attempt_id) -> int | None` — Who took the attempt, or ``None`` if there is no such attempt.
- `pending_descriptive_answers(db, attempt_id) -> list[PendingDescriptive]` — Answered descriptive questions of a submitted attempt not evaluated yet.
- `record_descriptive_evaluation(db, attempt_id, question_id, *, score, max_score, feedback) -> float` — Store a descriptive answer's evaluation in the attempt; returns the points earned.
- `score_breakdown(db, attempt_id) -> ScoreBreakdown` — The attempt's objective, descriptive and total score with an explanation.

### Data types

- `AttemptResult(attempt_id, quiz_id, user_id, score, max_score, submitted_at)`
- `ScoredAttempt(attempt_id, user_id, quiz_id, quiz_title, subject, topic, score, max_score, submitted_at)` — A submitted attempt with the subject and topic of the quiz it was taken at.
- `QuizListing(id, title, subject, topic, difficulty, channel_id, creator_id, created_at, question_count, attempt_count)` — A published, attemptable quiz as a recommendation shows it.
- `QuizInfo(id, title, subject, topic, difficulty, duration_minutes, channel_id, creator_id, status, is_adaptive, question_count)` — What another module may show about one quiz (a chat preview card, S11.2).
- `QuizContribution(id, title, created_at)` — One quiz the user contributed, for their profile's history (S01.2).

Also re-exported from the module's internals: `ATTEMPT_SCORED`, `AdaptiveAnswer`, `AdaptiveAnswerError`, `AttemptOutcome`, `NotSubmittedError`, `PendingDescriptive`, `ScoreBreakdown`, `ScorePart`, `ServedQuestion`.

## reputation

Reputation module (FR-01, FR-13).

- **Owns tables:** `reputation_events`, `badges`, `user_badges`
- **May call:** `accounts`
- **Called by:** `materials`, `profiles`, `questions`
- **Publishes events:** –
- **Subscribes to events:** –

### Routes

- `GET /api/v1/leaderboard`
- `GET /api/v1/reputation/me`
- `GET /api/v1/badges`

### Service functions

- `award(db, *, user_id, points, reason, source_type, source_id) -> None` — Record a reputation change, update the cached total and award any new badges.
- `total(db, user_id) -> int` — Return the user's total reputation points.
- `ensure_badge(db, code, name, description) -> int` — Return the id of the badge with ``code``, creating it if needed.
- `grant_badge(db, user_id, badge_id) -> None` — Award the badge to the user; does nothing if they already hold it.
- `badges_for(db, user_id) -> list[EarnedBadge]` — Badges the user has earned, most recent first (S01.2 profile).
- `record_peer_rating(db, *, contributor_id, rater_id, rating, source_type, source_id) -> int` — Bring the contributor's reputation in line with one peer's rating. Caller commits.
- `award_threshold_badges(db, user_id) -> list[str]` — Grant every badge whose threshold the user's total has reached; returns new codes.
- `events_for(db, user_id, *, limit, offset) -> tuple[list[ReputationEntry], int]` — The user's reputation events, newest first, and how many there are.
- `badge_codes_for(db, user_ids) -> dict[int, list[str]]` — Earned badge codes per user, in threshold order then by code.
- `leaderboard(db, *, limit, offset) -> tuple[list[LeaderboardEntry], int]` — Users with positive reputation, highest first, and how many there are.
- `rank_of(db, user_id) -> int | None` — The user's leaderboard rank, or ``None`` while they have no positive reputation.

### Data types

- `BadgeLevel(code, name, description, threshold)` — A badge awarded automatically once a user's reputation reaches ``threshold``.
- `EarnedBadge(code, name, description, earned_at)`
- `ReputationEntry(id, points, reason, source_type, source_id, created_at)` — One audited reputation change.
- `LeaderboardEntry(rank, user_id, display_name, username, reputation, badges)`
